sentences.text: 2. Sri R.Shashi Kumar, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioners' father namely Lakshmaiah was absolute owner of land bearing Sy.no.51/1, measuring to an extent 24 guntas and Sy.no.81/1 measuring 07 guntas, situated at Sigehalli village, Vemgal Hobli, Kolar District.
After his death petitioners became absolute owners of petition NC: 2023:KHC:45827 schedule properties.
Respondent no.2 acquired said lands for formation of industrial area under preliminary notification dated 06.07.2010, which was published under Gazette notification dated 07.07.2010 for said purpose.

3. It was submitted that though petitioner was entitled to higher compensation under consent award, without offering opportunity to avail same, General Award was passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO), which was under Sri V. L. Ramanji vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134056637/
2 challenge.

entities.text: Sri V. L. Ramanji vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was contended that under consent award, compensation was considerably higher than under General Award.
It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court allowed W.P.no.20457-463/2015 vide order 05.04.2016.
Relying upon same, sought for granting similar relief.

4. On other hand, Sri Yogesh D. Naik, learned AGA, for respondent no.1 and Sri P.V.Chandrashekar,
learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that no General Award appears to have been passed insofar as petitioners' land.

In case, petitioners furnish relevant documents such as title deeds etc., along with representation, respondent no.3 would consider same, in accordance with law,
within reasonable time.
Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
6. From above, it is seen that failure to pass consent award is due to non-furnishing of application along with supporting documents like title deeds etc. by petitioners.

In W.P.no.20457-463/2015,
this Court under similar circumstances had quashed General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award.
Said decision would squarely apply in this case also.

7. Accordingly, Writ petition is disposed of, impugned General Award dated 12.07.2017 bearing No.KIDB LAQ:2017/2018 at Annexure-'G' passed by respondent no.3 under Section 11 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in respect of petitioners' property, is quashed.

Respondent no.3 is directed to consider petitioners' case for passing consent award under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act within a period of three months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
However, it is made clear that if there were to be any dispute relating to title of lands in question, General Award passed shall stand revived.
Respondent no.3 is permitted to withdraw compensation, if any, deposited before Reference Court.

Sd/-

(b) Issue any suitable order, direction or writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent herein to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, etc.
